summary: Full verification of Manager Whisper P2 + AIAssistant Voice Mode. All 6 pytest tests in test_whisper.py pass green. Route ordering verified (/voice/calls/active resolves correctly, not swallowed by /{call_id}). Auth guard (401 without header) and validation (400 empty/oversized, 404 missing bridge) all confirmed via live curl + pytest. In-process ASGI happy-path verifies conversation.item.create with role=system + 'MANAGER WHISPER' prefix followed by response.create sent to mocked OpenAI WS, plus cross-tenant 403 guard. Frontend: /biz/voice loads with fallback 'No active calls' empty card, [data-testid=live-calls-panel] correctly absent when no calls. AIAssistant voice toggle switches text↔voice mode: [data-testid=ai-mic] + 'Tap and speak' appear, [data-testid=ai-toggle-speak] mute toggle appears, and toggling back restores [data-testid=ai-input] + [data-testid=ai-send].

issues: Badge text in JSX is 'Voice' (title case) styled uppercase by CSS class. Review-request spec said 'VOICE' badge — the visual output IS uppercase via .uppercase class, so acceptance criterion met. Just noting for future exact-text selector authors.

critical_code_review_comments: LIVE_BRIDGES is a module-global dict — will not survive multi-worker gunicorn/uvicorn setups. If the backend is scaled horizontally, whisper injection will only work when the whisper POST lands on the same worker holding the Twilio<->OpenAI WS. Consider a Redis pub/sub or single-worker deployment note.

whisper endpoint persists to db.voice_calls with $push but no upsert; if the call_doc row hasn't been inserted yet (race at very start of call), whisper text is lost from audit trail. Low risk given register_bridge is called AFTER voice_calls.insert_one in the WS handler.
seed_data_creation: None — in-process test uses AsyncMock() bridges injected into voice.LIVE_BRIDGES and clears after.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_whisper.py is the canonical whisper regression suite. Route ordering (active before /{id}) is critical — do not reorder. Voice mode UI requires Chrome/Edge (Web Speech API); playwright chromium supports it.
